Outcome: one `project_manager(action="update_task")` call persists every field it sends and leaves the other fields untouched — moving a card and scheduling it are not mutually exclusive.

## Finding (software_developer shift 1, 2026-11-17T13:05Z)

`update_task` does not merge: each call rewrites the fields it does NOT send from a stale/default copy, silently undoing the previous call. Reproduced on card `1c817139-19ce-43f9-ab37-df1ac9b7e3c4` (three consecutive calls, exact payloads):

1. `update_task(chat_id="1c817139-…", board="IT team", column="Blocked", status="onhold", progress=60)` → `changed_fields: [board, column, progress, status]`, task: `column "Blocked"`, `status "onhold"`, `progress 60`, **`wake_at null`**.
2. `update_task(chat_id="1c817139-…", wake_at="+1d")` → `changed_fields: [wake_at]`, task: `wake_at "2026-11-18T13:05:45Z"` **but `column "Review"`, `status "doing"`, `progress 40`** — the move from call 1 is gone.
3. `update_task(chat_id="1c817139-…", board="IT team", column="Blocked", status="onhold", progress=60)` → `changed_fields: [board, column, progress, status]`, task: `column "Blocked"`, `status "onhold"`, `progress 60`, **`wake_at null`** — the wake from call 2 is gone.

Net effect: a card cannot be both moved and scheduled; whatever is written last wins and the other write is discarded with no error. Same class as the `status_history[*].meta_data` defect (custom/wrong model copy is written back as the whole card).

## What to do (owner: software_developer)

1. Reproduce with the three calls above (any card, they are reversible).
2. In `project_manager_tools.py` / `task_manager.py`, load the persisted card, apply only the provided arguments, and write the merged object back. Never rebuild an unset field from a default.
3. Keep the existing validation (invalid column → rejected, not written).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A single call carrying both `column="Blocked"` and `wake_at="+1d"` yields `get_task` with `column: "Blocked"`, `status: "onhold"` **and** the new `wake_at` present.
2. A call that only sets `progress` leaves `column`, `status` and `wake_at` byte-identical.
3. A targeted regression test covers both (blocked today by `0dd3f3d4` — the suite does not collect).

Reference: `api/codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py`, `api/codx/junior/task_manager.py`.

## Second reproduction — a comment write also reverts the card state

The same non-merging write path is hit by `request_help` (comment), not only by `update_task`.

Timeline on card `1c817139-19ce-43f9-ab37-df1ac9b7e3c4` (all UTC, 2026-11-17):

| time | call | resulting `column` / `status` / `progress` / `wake_at` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 13:05:09 | `update_task(column="Blocked", status="onhold", progress=60)` | Blocked / onhold / 60 / null |
| 13:05:45 | `update_task(wake_at="+1d")` | **Review / doing / 40** / 2026-11-18T13:05:45Z |
| 13:05:56 | `update_task(column="Blocked", status="onhold", progress=60)` | Blocked / onhold / 60 / **null** |
| 13:06:57 | `request_help(comment="## State note after the QA block …")` | **Review / doing / 40** / null (`list_tasks` read-back) |

So a write that only appends a message restores the card to a pre-move snapshot: the move is undone by the comment. This makes the shift procedure itself unreliable — the author moves the card, comments the evidence, and the comment silently moves the card back.

**Add to the fix scope:** every write path (update, comment, and any future action) must load the persisted card, mutate in place, and save. The card must be read back after each write. Also check `list_tasks` vs `get_task` disagreement observed on the same card (`message_count` 11 via `get_task`, `1` via `list_tasks`) — either a stale index or a second copy of the card JSON being maintained.

Current effective state of card `1c817139`: `column "Review"`, `status "doing"`, `progress 40`. It is deliberately left in Review by this shift because repeated moves are reverted; the reviewer must move it to `Blocked` once this defect is fixed, or after the QA environment task `0dd3f3d4-5deb-4a8c-b36a-6f381f1cc91b` lands.
